results.title: The GPU Rental Market for Individuals: US Trends, Japan's Potential, and 2026 Outlook
highlights:
"Rent an H100 for just an hour, paid by credit card"—in the U.S., it is becoming commonplace for individual developers and small teams to rent NVIDIA AI GPUs on a per-second or per-minute pay-as-you-go basis. The options have rapidly expanded, ranging from services like RunPod, Vast.ai, Lambda, and Salad, to decentralized marketplaces often called the "Airbnb for GPUs," such as io.net and Akash. The on-demand market rate for an H100 at specialized providers has generally dropped to about $2–4/h (the aggregated average of 43+ providers is approximately $3.54/h), and through consumer GPU decentralized platforms like Salad, an RTX 4090 can be rented for ~$0.18/h (all data as of May 2026, details below).

...

The prices in this article are a snapshot as of May 2026. In principle, primary information confirmed on each company's official pricing page is prioritized, while assertions or third-party aggregations that could not be verified by primary sources are clearly labeled as " secondary information" or " unverified." Since GPU spot market rates and exchange rates fluctuate weekly, always check the latest prices on each company's site before use.

...

This layer is best suited for individuals, where a GPU can be up and running within minutes of registering a card. Below are representative prices (per GPU/hr) as of May 2026.

| Service | H100 SXM (On-demand) | Entry to Mid-range GPU | Billing / Payment | Reliability |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hyperstack | $2.40/h | A100 SXM $1.60 / L40 $1.00 / A6000 $0.50 | Per-minute / Stripe Card | Verified (matches official) |
| Paperspace (DigitalOcean) | $5.95/h | A6000 $1.89 / A4000 $0.76 | Per-hour / Free tier available | Verified (Updated 2026/5/30) |
| Salad | (Not provided) | RTX 4090 ~$0.18 / RTX 5090 ~$0.27 | Decentralized / Interrupt-tolerant | Secondary/Medium (Cannot re-acquire via 403) |
| RunPod | ~$1.99 (Community) – $2.39 (Secure) | RTX 4090 ~$0.34–0.69 / RTX 5090 ~$0.69–0.99 | Per-second/hour | Secondary / Unverified |
| Lambda | $4.29 (PCIe $3.29) | GH200 $2.29 | Per-minute / Free egress | Secondary / Unverified |

The individual prices for RunPod, Lambda, and Together AI are based on descriptions from primary sources but have not been re-verified during the verification phase of this article (secondary information/unverified). The entry-level pricing for Salad (from ~$0.02/h, RTX 5090 ~$0.27/h) is based on aggregator data because the official site blocks automated scraping; thus, the accuracy is medium.

The key takeaway is that providers like Hyperstack exist where you can rent an H100 for $2.40/h, billed by the minute, with just a card. Paperspace even provides a free tier (5GB) that automatically stops after 12 hours, creating a truly "hands-on" experience for individuals.

...

Do not confuse "host revenue" with "renter price."

...

- CoreWeave (Verified; matches official pricing): HGX H100 8GPU node $49.24/h (~$6.16 per GPU), H200 8GPU $50.44/h, A100 8GPU $21.60/h, B200 8GPU $68.80/h. L40 for inference starts at $1.25/h. Discounts of up to 60% are available via reservation, and spot discounts are approximately 55–60% off (e.g., $19.71 for H100 spot). While there is an on-demand 1GPU GH200 option ($6.50/h), it is not "completely inaccessible" to individuals, but it is Kubernetes-native and oriented towards scale/enterprise use cases.
- Genesis Cloud: High-performance tiers effectively require a 1-node (8GPU) minimum and sales inquiry. H100 on-demand is $2.19/h (the commonly seen $1.60/h figure refers to reserved/minimum node pricing). Smaller RTX cards are available for on-demand use.
- Together AI (Secondary/Unverified): Their core product is token-billed serverless inference ($0.0015–$4.50 per million tokens). They also provide dedicated GPU clusters, but these are high-priced, such as HGX H100 at $5.49/GPU/h, targeting teams and production environments.

## U.S. Market Price Structure — The Going Rates for H100 and Entry-Level GPUs

Looking at the numbers, the on-demand market for H100s is highly tiered based on the delivery model:

| Category | H100 On-Demand Rate |
| --- | --- |
| Consumer Decentralized (Spot/Interruptible) | Under $1.30 possible |
| Decentralized/Specialized Cloud | Starting from the $1.03–$2.49/h range |
| Specialty Providers (Self-Service) Core Range | ~$2–$4/h |
| Hyperscaler Market Rates | $4–$7+/h (AWS p5 actual $6.88, Azure $6.98, GCP ranges from $3–$11) |

Aggregated data from GetDeploying (43+ providers; secondary information) shows an average of approximately $3.54/h. It is solidly confirmed across multiple sources that specialty providers are 2 to 3 times cheaper than hyperscalers. Introl reports that H100 rates have fallen from a peak of around $8/h to the current $2.85–$3.50/h (a ~64% drop) (secondary information).

Entry-level perception (verified): RTX 4090 is well under $1/h, with Salad at ~$0.18/h and RunPod Community at ~$0.34/h. RTX 5090 is cheap on Salad at ~$0.27/h, while RunPod Secure is ~$0.99/h and Vast.ai market rates are ~$1.0–$1.2/h, hovering around or slightly above $1/h. Note that RTX 5090 (32GB) supply is tight as of May 2026, causing rapid price volatility. These cards are suitable for inference, image/video generation, small-scale fine-tuning (7B–30B), and 3D tasks. They are ill-suited for large-scale LLM training (video generation is considered safe with 32GB VRAM, and the local GPU VRAM shortage is what created this grassroots demand for cloud services).

1. On-Demand GPUs — billed per GPU-hour, hourly for the life of the instance. Published starting rates (October 2026): H100 SXM $3.19, H200 $3.99, B200 $5.99 per GPU-hour — the marketplace’s “Rent GPUs starting at” claim equals the H100 rate. Rates are refreshed weekly based on the best available rates from suppliers, but the rate displayed at instance creation is locked for that instance’s lifetime. No minimum commitment, no hidden or egress fees. B300 (Blackwell Ultra, 288 GB HBM3e) appears in the docs’ GPU lineup with no published per-hour rate.
2. Reserved — the same GPUs and setup at a discounted prepaid $/GPU/hour, paid in full up front for a fixed term; “longer terms unlock lower rates”. Minimum commitment from 1 week, with larger commitments arranged via the sales team; no early termination. Reservation Protection is now live and on by default: at the end of the term the instance converts to on-demand and bills at the current on-demand rate until you terminate it.
3. Private Cloud — dedicated single-tenant infrastructure on a custom contract, negotiated per deal on multi-month to multi-year commitments (“typically $1M+ deployments”) and billed separately from credits.
4. Hyperbolic Inference — billed per million tokens, with separate input, cached input and output rates per model, deducted from the credit balance. Eleven text and vision models are listed “as of October 21, 2026”, from $0.06/M input and $0.18/M output (deepseek-v4-flash-0731) up to $3.00/M input and $15.00/M output (kimi-k3). Errored requests are not charged, and thinking tokens bill as output.
5. Storage volumes — metered hourly per GB of provisioned capacity, at on-demand rates on total volume size regardless of capacity used or data transferred. No per-GB dollar rate is published on the captured surfaces.

Rates are “refreshed weekly based on the best available rates from suppliers on our platform”, so the per-hour price is dynamic. Node configuration for H100 / H200 is 8 GPUs per node with up to 160 vCPUs, up to 1.5 TB RAM and up to 24 TB local NVMe; multi-node clusters can use InfiniBand (up to 3.2 Tb/s, NDR / ConnectX-7). Hourly billing carries no hidden or egress fees, and failed instances are never charged; the marketplace promises notification “within 3 minutes if an instance fails”.

Between the 15 June and 4 August 2026 captures, Hyperbolic reset its published on-demand starting rates twice — and the second reset landed just two weeks after the first, not five. H100 SXM moved $1.50 → $2.89 → $3.19 (June → July → August), a cumulative +112.7% in seven weeks; H200 moved $2.40 → $3.49 → $3.99 (+66.3% cumulative); B200 moved $3.50 → $5.99 in July and then held flat in August (+71.1% cumulative, unchanged in the latest capture). Nothing about the pricing mechanism changed across either reset — the page still says rates are “refreshed weekly based on the best available rates from suppliers” — which is precisely the point: a marketplace rate that floats with aggregated third-party supply can float upward as hard as it floats down, repeatedly, without a repricing announcement, a migration path, or a grandfathering policy, because none of those artefacts exist in a spot model.

results.title: RTX 5090: Rent or Buy? The PRU 2500 Cost Breakdown
highlights:
Seventeen months after the RTX 5090 launched, the cloud rental market has stratified into four clean tiers. The current cross-market median is $0.65/hr, and the on-demand band sits in a tight $0.34 range across the major secure-cloud operators:

Spot / batch ($0.20–$0.30/hr) — Salad at $0.27, Vast.ai interruptible at $0.30. Can be reclaimed at any second, no SLA, consumer-PC reliability. Useful for fault-tolerant batch and embeddings.

Peer marketplace ($0.35–$0.70/hr) — Vast.ai on-demand and RunPod Community sit here, with the Vast.ai marketplace median around $0.36. Variable hardware, no SLA, per-host quality lottery.

Dedicated datacenter ($0.65–$1.00/hr) — Runcrate at $0.55, CloudRift at $0.65, NeevCloud and RunPod Community at $0.69, Lambda at $0.79, Vast.ai on-demand at $0.88, Fluence at $0.90, Spheron at $0.92, RunPod Secure at $0.99. This is where production workloads actually run.

Reserved / committed ($0.39–$0.55/hr) — Runcrate reserved at $0.39, Lambda 1-year, RunPod enterprise. A 30 to 50 percent discount against on-demand, in exchange for a multi-month capacity commitment.

The 3.7x spread between $0.27 and $0.99 is not arbitrary. It is the sum of distinct cost layers: power and cooling (~$0.07/hr), host margin (~$0.13/hr), verification premium (~$0.08/hr), datacenter facility (~$0.18/hr), NVIDIA commercial-use licensing (~$0.14/hr), SLA and networking (~$0.12/hr), and provider margin (~$0.27/hr). When you pay $0.99 instead of $0.27, you are paying for those layers, not for a better GPU.

...

Across three years and 24/7 utilization the PRU 2500 with 8x5090 GPUs consumes 210,240 GPU-hours. Multiplying out the four tier benchmarks against this configuration gives the following picture.

PRU 2500 with 8x5090 GPUs at $99,999:

Spot $0.27/hr: 3-year rental = $56,765. Renting saves $43,234 — on the spot floor, with all the same SLA caveats.

Reserved $0.39/hr: 3-year rental = $81,994. Renting saves $18,005, again with a multi-month capacity commitment and no owned hardware.

Market median $0.65/hr: 3-year rental = $136,656. The PRU 2500 w/5090s saves $36,657.

Vast.ai on-demand $0.88/hr: 3-year rental = $185,011. The PRU 2500 w/5090s saves $85,012.

RunPod Secure $0.99/hr: 3-year rental = $208,138. The PRU 2500 w/5090s saves $108,139.

The price story does not collapse. It shifts. Against marketplace spot pricing, the PRU 2500 w/5090s is more expensive on a pure dollar-per-hour basis. Against the cross-market median and every production tier above it, the PRU 2500 w/5090s is tens to hundreds of thousands of dollars cheaper across three years — and at the end you own the silicon.

results.title: The cheapest way to run RTX 5090 and H200 inference without AWS — a real cost comparison - DEV Community
highlights: running AI inference on AWS for high-end GPUs is expensive and most teams stay there longer than they should. ran a proper cost comparison when we were evaluating options. AWS H200 on-demand pricing: $5 to $6.50 per hour depending on configuration and region. RTX 5090 on-demand: not reliably available, requires reserved capacity or waitlisting. alternatives i actually evaluated: Vast.ai — cheapest headline prices. RTX 5090 and H200 available but node quality and availability vary by day. p99 cold start is rough on busy days because of the marketplace model. RunPod — H200 on-demand around $4.30/hr. more predictable than Vast.ai. still 2x the price of the best option i found. Lambda Labs — solid but waitlisted for RTX 5090 in my experience. Yotta Labs — RTX 5090 at $0.65/hr, H200 at $2.10/hr. these have matched actual billing in several months of use, no egress surprises. the multi-provider pooling also means availability during demand spikes is better than single-provider options. the H200 comparison specifically: $2.10/hr on Yotta vs $4.30/hr on RunPod vs $5-6.50/hr on AWS. for inference-heavy workloads on H200 without committed reservations, this is a significant difference that compounds over time. the "it depends on workload" caveat is always technically true. for on-demand inference-heavy workloads on high-end SKUs without committed reservations, the numbers have been consistently in Yotta's favor over several months of production use.

results.title: Средний чек GPU-серверов для ИИ вырос до 2,3 млн рублей
highlights:
Средняя месячная стоимость за выделенную инфраструктуру с GPU-ускорителями для задач ИИ и машинного обучения за пять месяцев 2026 года выросла на 64% по сравнению с аналогичным периодом 2025 года и достигла 2,3 млн руб. против около 1,4 млн руб. годом ранее, следует из данных облачного и bare metal-провайдера «Рег.Облако».

Сейчас 33% заказов на GPU-серверы приходится на задачи искусственного интеллекта и машинного обучения, 30% — на рендеринг, 25% — на тестирование и разработку, еще 12% — на обработку данных, говорят в компании. Такой профиль спроса существенно отличается от классической модели аренды серверов под корпоративные порталы и ИТ-системы.

...

(см. “Ъ” от 24 января). По оценкам, в 2026 году он может вырасти вдвое.

«Наша оценка роста также на уровне 60%. Это подтверждается подорожанием продвинутых GPU-серверов на 30–50%, ростом цены оперативной памяти в 10 раз, а около 60% спроса рынка — это задачи ИИ/ML», — отмечают в пресс-службе MWS Cloud. При этом в компании также подтверждают, что количество серверов существенно не изменилось.

results.title: How do you develop a sovereign AI strategy in a market with huge competition for energy and an 85% GPU price premium? A thoughtful piece this week from Heritiér Bahizi and great … | Sarah Rees
highlights:
**Reshared from Signwl:**
> In The New Times (Rwanda) this week Heritiér Bahizi outlines potential options for sovereign AI in a region with high competition for energy.
>
> Sarah Rees highlights how low GPU supply is currently impacting pricing: renting an NVIDIA H100 in Africa costs 85% more than the global average ($13.55 per hour vs $7.32) based on our May 2026 data.
>
> Building out supply is key, and in markets where energy is tight, an inference-focused buildout could enable sovereign AI on lower-energy hardware. An opportunity to rethink the traditional hyperscaler model for the region.
